label.text: Make one for each phone, computer or app, so that losing one means revoking only its password. You see the password once, when it is made.

Your phone and desktop apps read and change your calendars, tasks, contacts and files here: the calendar, contacts and files apps the device has, logged in with your username and an app password. An app password works only for sync; it does not open this site, and your second factor stays on your own sign-in.
Enter it in the device now, as the password of the account with the username ${syncUsername}. It is shown only this once; make another if you lose it.

link.confirmation: Revoke the app password of ${name}? That device stops syncing until it gets a new one.

label.text: No devices yet · Make an app password for the first one

Settings, Calendar (or Contacts), Accounts, Add Account, Other: Add CalDAV Account for calendars and reminders, Add CardDAV Account for contacts. Server: ${addresses.serverHost}; User Name: ${syncUsername}; Password: an app password. The account finds your calendars, tasks (in Reminders) and contact books.
Files: in the Files app, the menu (…) then Connect to Server, with ${addresses.filesUrl}.

System Settings, Internet Accounts, Add Account, Add Other Account: CalDAV account and CardDAV account, type Manual, with ${syncUsername}, an app password and the server ${addresses.serverHost}. Calendar, Reminders and Contacts then show them.
Files: in the Finder, Go, Connect to Server (Command-K), with ${addresses.filesUrl}.

Install DAVx⁵ (from Google Play or F-Droid), add an account with Login with URL and user name: the URL ${davUrl}, ${syncUsername} and an app password. Pick the calendars, task lists (with jtx Board or Tasks.org) and contact books to sync; they show in the phone's own Calendar and Contacts apps.
Files: a file manager with WebDAV (Material Files, Solid Explorer) with ${addresses.filesUrl}.

Files: File Explorer, This PC, Map network drive, Connect to a Web site that you can use to store your documents and pictures, with ${addresses.filesUrl}, then your username and an app password. The server must be reached over HTTPS.
Calendars and contacts: Thunderbird (below), or Outlook with a CalDAV synchronizer add-in.

Calendar: New Calendar, On the Network, with ${syncUsername} and the location ${davUrl}; Find Calendars lists them all. Contacts: New Address Book, Add CardDAV Address Book, with the same location. Use an app password when it asks.

GNOME Online Accounts and KDE accounts take the CalDAV and CardDAV address ${davUrl}. A file manager opens davs:// with the WebDAV address; rclone and other tools take it as a WebDAV remote. SFTP, when it is served: ${addresses.sftpUrl || 'not served here'}, logged in with the app password.
